---

## Zone 1

The two lines are the card's own, and they are not negotiable in shape because `checkLedger` enforces the pairing:
1. `// authz-row: grant-validity-window` in the proof file's header;
2. `proof: 'delegation-of-duty.dogfood.test.ts'` on the `grant-validity-window` row.

## Zone 2 — my assumptions

1. I assume this is genuinely two lines and no test content changes. If citing the proof makes `checkLedger` demand anything further (a `HIGH_RISK` classification, a `covers` entry), that is a finding to report — ⛔ do not satisfy a new demand by editing the matrix's risk classification, which is a different decision on a different card.
2. I assume the row stays `state: 'enforced'` and gains a proof, rather than changing state. The card frames this as an upgrade from "unit-proven, e2e exists but uncited" to "cited end-to-end proof" — the state should not move.

## Gates

Derive with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs <your actual paths>` once the diff is real; expect the `packages/qa/dogfood/**` liveness family and the test-file convention family. **Report by CI JOB name, not by the local command.** Required checks are **six**: `TypeScript Type Check`, `ESLint`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`.

⛔ Never weaken a gate to get green. ⛔ No model identifier in any pushed artifact.

## ACCEPT — PM `domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `session_012WKSnqAaoqtW3QX7SSf1Vk`

PR **#9439** at `2e13bcd1f` (two commits, 4 lines total). Enqueued; all six required checks running clean, nothing red. Labels `size/xs` + `tests` + `skip-changeset` — the right disposition for a ledger-attribution change with no shipped behaviour.

### The reverse verification is what makes this card safe, and it was done properly

This card's entire safety argument is "the gate will catch a broken pairing", so measuring that once is the deliverable. Direction predicted in writing first, then the header marker was deleted and the gate named the missing side verbatim:

> `grant-validity-window: proof does not claim this row — add `authz-row: grant-validity-window` to delegation-of-duty.dogfood.test.ts, or stop citing it`

Restored, green again. That converts the safety argument from an assumption into a measurement, which is the difference between a two-line change being safe and merely looking safe.

Both Zone 2 assumptions held: `checkLedger` demanded nothing beyond the marker/citation pair (no `HIGH_RISK`, no `covers`), and the row stayed `state: 'enforced'`.

### The rework, and why it mattered

The first commit added the citation while leaving the row's own note ending with *"It is not cited here … filed as a follow-up"* — a sentence that went false the instant the line three above it landed, and whose "follow-up" was this very card. That is the same **declared ≠ actual** shape this ledger exists to record, sitting inside the ledger. Verified corrected on the branch:

> *"Unlike those rows an end-to-end proof **EXISTS and is now cited (#9377)** … and **its header now claims this row back — the #7976 mutual-attribution contract is satisfied.**"*

It now states **both directions** of the pairing, which is more than I asked for and is the right amount. Everything else in the note — the `HIGH_RISK` reasoning, the unit pins, the #8802 note — is untouched, confirmed by a scoped diff showing exactly one changed line.

Worth crediting: when the Edit tool's string match failed on an escaped-apostrophe JS literal, the dev located the target with a `count == 1` substring assertion rather than loosening the match — the failure mode there would have been silently rewriting neighbouring prose in a 2000-character note.

### Two scoping calls, both proportionate and both *stated*

Neither run covered everything, and in both cases the dev said so with a reason rather than implying full coverage:
1. **Two test files instead of the full ~111-file dogfood suite** — comment/attribution-only diff, the one cross-file consumer (`checkLedger`'s attribution scan, which reads every `*.dogfood.test.ts` header) run in full at 27/27, and the required `Dogfood Regression Gate` runs the whole suite in CI regardless.
2. **No second full-workspace build / `check:type-check-debt` re-measure for the follow-up** — the diff is one string literal inside an already-typechecked file, so no new symbols and no structural change; the prior full run covered that surface at head−1, and `checkLedger` plus the ESLint family were re-run over the two-commit total.

Both are the honest version of "I did not re-run everything". A scoped run that names its scope is not the same act as a scoped run that hides it.
